metadata.title: Hypertension: Conducting Studies of Drugs to Treat Patients on a Background of Multiple Antihypertensive Drugs Guidance for Industry
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 27 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 28 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 29 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 30 not required. 31
candidates.context: Sponsors have approached FDA to discuss development programs for drugs intended to treat 21 resistant hypertension , which sponsors have defined as hypertension not adequately controlled 22 by maximally tolerated doses of three or more antihypertensive drugs with different mechanisms 23 of action. FDA encourages development of additional classes of drugs for hypertension, 24 particularly classes of drugs that demonstrate effects when added to currently available therapies. 25

candidates.statement: • Demonstrate superiority to another (or more than one) antihypertensive drug (active 82 comparator) in reducing blood pressure in hypertensive patients already receiving 83 maximum doses of three or more antihypertensive drugs with different mechanisms of 84 action. This would result in a claim that the new drug is superior to the specific active 85 comparator drug for the treatment of hypertension, to lower blood pressure. The active 86 comparator should differ in mechanism of action from the mechanisms of the background 87 medications, and the dose(s) of the active comparator would have to be the maximum 88
candidates.context: • Demonstrate superiority to placebo in reducing blood pressure in hypertensive patients on 75 appropriate doses of three or more antihypertensive drugs with different mechanisms of 76 action. This would result in a claim that the new drug is indicated for the treatment of 77 hypertension, to lower blood pressure. The background medications and the range of 78 doses taken during the study, as well as the added effect of the new drug, would be 79 described in the CLINICAL STUDIES section of the resulting labeling. 80 Contains Nonbinding Recommendations Draft — Not for Implementation
